name: Accuracy
definition: The share of predictions that are correct; misleading when classes are imbalanced.

name: Addition Rule
definition: When alternatives are mutually exclusive, the number of outcomes is the sum of the counts.

name: Antiderivative
definition: A function whose derivative is the given function; differentiation run backwards.

name: Applications of the Definite Integral
definition: Using integration to compute areas, volumes, lengths and accumulated quantities.

name: Artificial Neuron
definition: A unit computing a weighted sum of inputs followed by a non-linear activation.

name: Averaging and Majority Vote
definition: The simplest combination rules: average the predicted numbers, or take the most frequent predicted class.

name: Backpropagation
definition: Computing the gradient of the loss with respect to every weight by applying the chain rule backwards through the layers.

name: Bagging
definition: Training each member on a bootstrap resample to decorrelate their errors and cut variance.

name: Baseline
definition: The trivial predictor any real model must beat before its score means anything.

name: Bayes' Rule
definition: The formula inverting a conditional probability, turning likelihood and prior into posterior.

name: Big-O Notation
definition: A notation bounding a function's growth from above up to a constant factor, used to compare rates of change.

name: Adaptive Boosting
definition: Fitting members in sequence, each concentrating on the examples its predecessors got wrong.

name: The Number of Elements in a Finite Set
definition: Counting a finite set, including the inclusion–exclusion correction for overlapping parts.

name: Cartesian Product
definition: The set of all ordered pairs drawn from two sets, the formal model of independent choices.

name: Cauchy Mean Value Theorem
definition: A two-function generalisation of the mean value theorem, the basis for L'Hôpital's rule.

name: Classification
definition: Supervised prediction of a discrete class label.

name: Matrix of a System of Linear Equations
definition: The matrix that holds the coefficients of an SLE, optionally augmented with the right-hand side column, so that the system can be manipulated as a single object instead of as separate equations.

name: Combination
definition: A selection of objects where order does not matter; the binomial coefficient counts them.

name: Combinatorics in Probability Problems
definition: Computing probabilities of equally likely outcomes by counting favourable and total cases.

name: Conditional Probability
definition: The probability of an event given that another has occurred, obtained by restricting the event space.

name: Confusion Matrix
definition: The table of predicted against actual classes, from which most classification metrics are derived.

name: Continuity on a Closed Interval
definition: A function is continuous on a closed interval when small changes of argument produce small changes of value throughout it, which guarantees strong global properties.

name: Convergence of a Series
definition: A series converges when its partial sums approach a finite limit.

name: Tests for Convergence
definition: The standard criteria — comparison, ratio, root, integral — for deciding convergence without summing.

name: Convergent Sequence
definition: A sequence that has a finite limit; such sequences are bounded and their limits respect arithmetic.

name: Convexity
definition: A function is convex when its graph lies below its chords; convexity is what makes minimisation well behaved.

name: Convolutional Operation
definition: Sliding a shared small filter across the input so that the same local pattern is detected anywhere.

name: Cross-Validation
definition: Rotating the held-out fold over the data to get a more stable performance estimate.

name: The Curse of Dimensionality
definition: In high dimensions data becomes sparse and distances lose contrast, undermining methods that rely on proximity.

name: Data Augmentation
definition: Enlarging the training set with label-preserving transformations of existing examples.

name: Data Compression
definition: Representing data with fewer numbers while preserving what matters.

name: DBSCAN
definition: Density-based clustering that finds arbitrarily shaped clusters and labels sparse points as noise.

name: Decision Tree
definition: A predictor that splits the feature space by recursive threshold questions.

name: Deep Learning
definition: Learning with many-layered networks that build their own representations of the input.

name: Definite Integral
definition: A number attached to a function on an interval, interpretable as signed area under its graph.

name: Derivative
definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function, defined as the limit of its difference quotient.

name: Determinant
definition: A single number computed from a square matrix that reports whether the matrix is invertible: a zero determinant means the transformation collapses space and cannot be undone.

name: Geometric Meaning of the Determinant
definition: For a 2×2 matrix the determinant is the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by its columns, so its magnitude is the area scaling factor and its sign records whether orientation is flipped.

name: Differentiable Function
definition: A function possessing a derivative at every point of an interval; differentiability implies continuity.

name: Differential of a Function
definition: The linear part of a function's increment, the formal expression of local linear approximation.

name: Differentiation Rules
definition: The algebraic rules — sum, product, quotient and chain — that let derivatives be computed without returning to the limit.

name: Domain of Convergence
definition: The set of arguments for which a power series converges.

name: Dropout
definition: Randomly disabling units during training so the network cannot rely on any single path.

name: Elementary Row Operations
definition: The three reversible moves on a matrix — swapping two rows, scaling a row by a non-zero number, and adding a multiple of one row to another — that change the matrix without changing the solution set of the system it represents.

name: Ensemble Learning
definition: Combining several models so their errors partly cancel and the whole beats any part.

name: Cauchy (ε–δ) Definition of a Limit
definition: The formal definition: for every ε there is a δ such that arguments within δ of the point map to values within ε of the limit.

name: Euler Diagram
definition: A picture of sets as regions, used to reason about their overlaps.

name: Event
definition: A subset of the event space, so that operations on events are operations on sets.

name: Event Space
definition: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment, the universe in which probability is defined.

name: Expected Value
definition: The probability-weighted average of a random variable, its long-run mean.

name: F1 / Dice Score
definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number balancing the two.

name: Feed-Forward Network
definition: A network of neuron layers passing signals in one direction from input to output.

name: Graphing Functions
definition: Assembling limits, derivatives and convexity into a full qualitative picture of a function's graph.

name: Jordan–Gauss Method (Gaussian Elimination)
definition: The systematic procedure of applying elementary row operations to bring a matrix to row-echelon form, and thereby to solve a system of linear equations by a fixed algorithm rather than ad-hoc tricks.

name: Geometric Transformations as Matrices
definition: The correspondence between matrices and geometric motions of the plane: applying a matrix to the coordinate vectors of a figure moves the figure, so composing motions becomes multiplying matrices.

name: Heine (Sequential) Definition of a Limit
definition: An equivalent definition of a function limit stated through the limits of all sequences approaching the point.

name: Hierarchical Clustering
definition: Building a nested tree of clusters by repeatedly merging or splitting groups.

name: Higher-Order Derivative
definition: The result of differentiating repeatedly; the second derivative measures curvature.

name: Holistic View of Evaluation
definition: Judging a model by the whole picture of metrics, baselines and error structure rather than one score.

name: Improper Integral
definition: An integral over an unbounded interval or of an unbounded function, defined as a limit of ordinary integrals.

name: Indefinite Integral
definition: The family of all antiderivatives of a function, differing by a constant.

name: Independent Events
definition: Events where knowing one occurred does not change the probability of the other.

name: Integration by Parts
definition: Trading one integral for another using the product rule in reverse.

name: Integration by Substitution
definition: Changing variable in an integral so that it matches a known antiderivative; the chain rule reversed.

name: Cauchy's Intermediate Value Theorem
definition: A function continuous on a closed interval attains every value between its endpoint values.

name: Explicit Inverse Formula for a 2×2 Matrix
definition: The closed-form expression that gives the inverse of a 2×2 matrix directly from its four entries and its determinant, with no elimination needed.

name: Inverse Matrix
definition: The matrix that undoes another: multiplying a matrix by its inverse gives the identity. It exists only for square matrices that are non-degenerate.

name: Finding an Inverse by the Jordan–Gauss Method
definition: Computing an inverse by row-reducing the matrix alongside the identity until the original becomes the identity and the identity becomes the inverse.

name: K-Means
definition: Partitioning data into k clusters by alternately assigning points to nearest centroids and recomputing them.

name: K-Nearest Neighbours
definition: Predicting from the labels of the closest training examples, with no explicit training step.

name: L1 Regularization
definition: Penalising the sum of absolute weights, which drives some exactly to zero and selects features.

name: L2 Regularization
definition: Penalising the sum of squared weights, shrinking them smoothly toward zero.

name: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
definition: On any interval a differentiable function has a point whose derivative equals the average rate of change across the interval.

name: L'Hôpital's Rule
definition: A technique for evaluating indeterminate limits by differentiating numerator and denominator separately.

name: Limit of a Function at a Point
definition: The value a function approaches as its argument approaches a given point, independently of the value at that point.

name: Limit of a Sequence
definition: The value a sequence approaches arbitrarily closely as the index grows without bound.

name: Linear Equation
definition: An equation in which every unknown appears only to the first power and is not multiplied by another unknown. It is the atom the whole course is built from.

name: Thinking in Terms of Linear Models
definition: The habit the course is ultimately aiming at: recognising when a situation with many quantities changing at once can be posed and solved linearly, rather than memorising procedures.

name: Linear Regression
definition: Fitting a linear function of the features by minimising squared error.

name: Linear Space (Vector Space)
definition: The abstract setting in which addition and scalar multiplication obey a fixed list of rules; recognising it is what lets the same reasoning transfer from arrows to data tables to functions.

name: Little-o Notation
definition: A notation stating that one function is asymptotically negligible relative to another.

name: Logical Operations
definition: Negation, conjunction, disjunction and implication, which combine propositions into compound statements.

name: Logical Proposition
definition: A statement that is definitely either true or false, the atom of formal reasoning.

name: Maclaurin Series
definition: The Taylor series taken at zero.

name: Matrix
definition: A rectangular table of numbers arranged in rows and columns, used to store coefficients, data sets or transformations compactly.

name: Matrix Addition
definition: Adding two matrices of identical dimensions entry by entry.

name: Modelling Real Situations with Vectors and Matrices
definition: The practice of translating a real problem — a small economic balance, a data-analysis task — into vectors and matrices so that it becomes a solvable system.

name: Matrix Multiplication
definition: Combining two matrices into a third whose entries are dot products of rows with columns; it corresponds to performing one transformation after another and is not commutative.

name: Matrix Transposition
definition: Reflecting a matrix across its main diagonal so that rows become columns; the operation behind symmetric matrices and many identities.

name: Matrix–Vector Multiplication
definition: Applying a matrix to a vector to obtain a new vector; this is the operation that turns a matrix into a transformation and lets an SLE be written as a single equation.

name: Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
definition: A continuous function attains its average value over an interval at some interior point.

name: Multiplication Rule
definition: When choices are made in sequence, the number of outcomes is the product of the counts.

name: Building Negations to Claims
definition: Turning a statement, including quantified ones, into its correct denial — the skill behind complementary events.

name: Newton–Leibniz Formula
definition: The fundamental link: a definite integral equals the increment of any antiderivative across the interval.

name: t-SNE / UMAP
definition: Non-linear dimensionality reduction aimed at preserving local neighbourhoods for visualisation.

name: The Number e
definition: The limit of (1+1/n)^n, the base of the natural exponential and logarithm.

name: One-Sided Limit
definition: The limit taken as the argument approaches a point from only the left or only the right.

name: Overfitting
definition: Fitting noise in the training data so that performance on unseen data degrades.

name: Principal Component Analysis
definition: Projecting data onto the directions of greatest variance, found from the eigenstructure of its covariance matrix.

name: Permutation
definition: An arrangement of objects where order matters.

name: A Posteriori Probability
definition: The updated probability of a hypothesis after evidence has been observed.

name: Power Series
definition: A series in powers of the variable, which behaves like a polynomial inside its region of convergence.

name: Precision
definition: The share of predicted positives that are actually positive.

name: Probability
definition: A number between 0 and 1 assigned to an event, measuring how likely it is.

name: Rules of Probability
definition: The axioms and their consequences: complement, addition for unions, monotonicity.

name: Random Distribution
definition: The assignment of probabilities to the values a random variable can take.

name: Random Forest
definition: Bagged decision trees with additional random feature subsampling at each split.

name: Random Variable
definition: A numerical quantity whose value is determined by the outcome of a random experiment.

name: Recall
definition: The share of truly positive cases the model retrieves.

name: Reflection (Symmetry)
definition: A transformation mirroring the plane across a line, expressible as a matrix and reversing orientation.

name: Regression
definition: Supervised prediction of a continuous numeric value.

name: Regularization
definition: Deliberately constraining a model to reduce overfitting at the cost of some training fit.

name: ROC / AUC
definition: The curve of true against false positive rates over all thresholds, and the area beneath it.

name: Rolle's Theorem
definition: A function continuous on a closed interval, differentiable inside it and equal at the endpoints has a stationary point strictly inside.

name: Rotation
definition: A transformation turning the plane about a point by a fixed angle, expressible as a matrix built from sine and cosine.

name: Row-Echelon Form
definition: A staircase shape for a matrix in which each leading entry sits strictly to the right of the one above it, making the solution of the corresponding system readable almost directly.

name: Scalar Multiplication
definition: Multiplying every entry of a vector or matrix by the same number, which stretches, shrinks or flips it without changing its shape.

name: Scaling
definition: A transformation stretching or shrinking the plane along its axes, the simplest case of a matrix acting geometrically.

name: Second Derivative Test
definition: Classifying a stationary point as a minimum or maximum by the sign of the second derivative there.

name: Sequence
definition: An ordered infinite list of numbers indexed by the natural numbers.

name: Series
definition: The formal sum of infinitely many terms, studied through the limit of its partial sums.

name: Set
definition: A collection of distinct objects considered as one whole.

name: Set Operations
definition: Union, intersection, difference and complement, the operations mirrored later by operations on events.

name: Solution Set of an SLE
definition: The full set of assignments satisfying a system: it may be empty, a single point, or an infinite family, and which case holds can be read off the row-echelon form.
aliases: consistency of a system|solutions for SLE

name: Solving an SLE via the Inverse Matrix
definition: Writing a square system as a single matrix equation and solving it by multiplying both sides by the inverse — an alternative strategy to elimination.

name: Special Limits
definition: The small catalogue of standard limits that serve as building blocks for evaluating harder ones.

name: Special Matrices
definition: Named matrix shapes that behave in particular ways — identity, zero, diagonal, square, symmetric — which act as the reference points for later operations.

name: Stacking and Blending
definition: Training a further model to combine the predictions of the base models.

name: Standard Deviation
definition: The square root of the variance, expressing spread in the units of the variable.

name: Subset
definition: A set all of whose elements belong to another set.

name: Supervised Learning
definition: Learning a mapping from inputs to known target values using labelled examples.

name: System of Linear Equations (SLE)
definition: A finite collection of linear equations that must hold simultaneously for the same set of unknowns; a solution is any assignment of values satisfying all of them at once.

name: Taylor Series
definition: The power series generated by a function's derivatives at a point.

name: Taylor's Formula
definition: An approximation of a smooth function near a point by a polynomial built from its derivatives, with a controlled remainder.

name: Total Probability Law
definition: Decomposing an event's probability across a partition of the event space; the chain rule of probability.

name: Train/Validation Split
definition: Holding out part of the data to estimate performance on examples not used for fitting.

name: Training Loop
definition: The repeated cycle of forward pass, loss evaluation, gradient computation and weight update.

name: Truth Table
definition: An exhaustive table of a compound statement's value for every assignment of its parts.

name: Unsupervised Learning
definition: Finding structure in data without target labels.

name: Variance
definition: The expected squared deviation from the mean, measuring spread.

name: Vector
definition: An ordered tuple of numbers treated as a single algebraic object that can be added to another vector and scaled by a number; geometrically an arrow with direction and length.

name: Vector Addition
definition: Adding two vectors componentwise to produce a third vector of the same size.

name: Weierstrass's Theorem
definition: A function continuous on a closed bounded interval is bounded and attains a maximum and a minimum on it.

name: Weight Decay
definition: Shrinking weights at every update step, the optimisation-side view of L2 penalty.
